body: docs-stamp-rerun-after-dropped-claim: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs:cmd_stamp (L890-L946) writes each docspec's state (L940-L942) before review.record_closes (L944), so a stop between them leaves new stamps and ledgers with no closed-record entry, and a rerun is allowed. later_commits_bearing (L876-L887) builds ledgers from read_state, i.e. the ledger the first pass already rewrote (planned_ledgers L581-L582), plus this run's held claims. A docspec counts as bearing (bearing_docspecs L585-L598) from change_reasons on its references and listed classes, or from a ledger claim whose file changed between the planned commit and the parent of --commit. ledger_after (L859-L867) drops a claim whose doc file is gone or whose recheck this run cut. So where the first pass stamped a docspec at the planned commit only because of such a claim, the rerun no longer finds it bearing, sets new_stamp to --commit (L915-L917), and, since old_stamp (the planned commit) differs, diffs planned..parent for stale claims (L919-L923). The fixer's narrow guard is the old_stamp != new_stamp test at L919; the filed problem still matches the code. Mechanism worth giving the author: in the residual case no remaining ledger claim rests on a file changed in planned..parent (any such claim would have made the docspec bearing on the rerun too), and change_reasons does not read the ledger, so the planned..parent diff drops nothing and the rerun loses no recheck; the only difference from the first pass is the stamp value (planned vs --commit), i.e. the rerun is not idempotent, and the next docs window opens later for that docspec. Corpus: decision:docspec-stamp-opens-the-window says the stamp is 'the commit at which its documentation last passed a documentation sprint' and that 'The stamp, the claim ledger, and the owner's worked example are run state ... written only by the documentation sprint's tool'; decision:documentation-claim-ledger says 'the ledger never holds a claim no checker confirmed at its stamp'; story:keep-documentation-current promises documentation that describes the product as it stands. None says what a rerun after a stop must stamp. Harm: no accept-list entry clearly covers the residual case as analysed above (A1 half-changed state is arguable: a stop between write_state and record_closes leaves state no complete run would produce only where the rerun stamps differently); state it as the owner's choice. Options: A. record the writing documentation sprint in each docspec's run state and have a rerun keep the planned-commit stamp that sprint wrote; cost: a new run-state field every docspec's state carries, and a run-state format change (stored state, a release boundary) for a rare stop. B. read each docspec's pre-stamp state from the closing commit (--commit) and stamp from it; cost: a git read per docspec on every stamp, and the closing commit holds the pre-stamp doc-state only because the owner commits before stamping, which the stamp must then assume. C. keep the narrow guard; cost: a rerun after a stop between the state write and the close record may stamp at --commit where the first pass stamped at the planned commit, which by the analysis above loses no recheck. D (filer missed): make the stamp atomic with the close, writing every doc-state file and the closed-record entry as one temp-then-rename step per plumbline-coding rule 3.1, so no rerun follows a partial stamp; cost: a stop mid-stamp still needs a rerun when the rename sequence itself spans several files. Siblings: none of this batch.

body: closed-record-ledger-rollback-on-failed-conversion: Evidence, re-verified in the working tree (uncommitted ninth intake-drain sprint work): plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up:convert_moving (L4220-4250) calls record_archived (L4224) before move_all (L4226); on any failure its finally block calls move_back, then unrecord_moved_back(recorded) (L4241). true-up:unrecord_moved_back (L4442-4451) keeps each name whose file no longer stands at os.path.join(ARCHIVE_DIR, name) and calls carried_review().unrecord_closes; note that this lexists probe reads the archive path it just moved out of. scripts/review:unrecord_closes (L1946-1954) rewrites the ledger under its lock, dropping the named entries. The filed facts hold. Mechanism: (1) a conversion moves files to fixed paths (true-up:conversion_pairs L4201-4206 joins history with each source name), so a retry of a failed conversion records the same names again; (2) scripts/review:record_closes (L1933-1937) refuses any entry the ledger already lists ('the closed-record ledger ... already lists ...'), so with no rollback every later /ok refuses at the retried conversion unless something treats the stale name as free. Corpus: decision:archive-read-by-nothing says 'Each archive step writes the bookkeeping before it moves a file into the archive, and picks the name it moves a file to from the closed-record ledger and the other live records, never by looking at what the archive holds'; decision:closing-commit-baseline says the ledger 'also lists each name true-up moved into the archive, so an archive step picks a free name without reading the archive'. No artifact says the ledger is append-only, and none says what a failed conversion leaves in it: the corpus is silent on the failure path. Harm without a rollback: A3 (later /ok fails, a state where later use fails) under option C's absence. Options: A (built) the ledger rolls back with the files; cost: the ledger loses its append-only shape for one path, and the corpus should say so in archive-read-by-nothing; the rollback's lexists probe touches the archive. B a later conversion treats a ledger name with no file at its archive path as free; cost: it probes the archive, against archive-read-by-nothing's 'never by looking at what the archive holds'. C a later conversion picks a name the ledger does not hold; cost: conversion paths stop being fixed, so drafts and the problem text of issues that cite history paths name the wrong file, and the ledger keeps a name no file holds. A fourth option the filer missed: record the names after a successful move instead of before (no rollback needed); cost: breaks archive-read-by-nothing's 'bookkeeping before the move' and a crash between move and record leaves files the ledger does not list (A1). Sibling: true-up-archive-moves-fail-owned-paths-check (its check must follow whichever shape convert_moving takes).

preflight-pass-counted-per-machine: Evidence, re-verified in the working tree (uncommitted ninth intake-drain sprint work): plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:stage_preflight (L5310-5333) files no preflight only where plan['budget'] carries a preflight mark, equals the scenario list's budget, and passed_here(root) == unmarked(plan['budget']) (L5313-5315). tests:passed_here (L5280-5286) reads .ok-planner/.cache/tests-preflight.json, git-ignored; tests:record_passed_here (L5290-5298) writes it under machine_lock when the sprint's latest preflight closed done. The tool's help text (tests L480-488) states the per-machine reading. The filed facts hold. Mechanism: (1) the committed preflight mark on the budget travels with the tree to every clone, while the cache record stays on one machine; (2) after an upgrade every machine, this one included, has no cache record, so each runs one preflight in its next tested sprint even where the committed budget already passed. Corpus: decision:test-stack-budgeted-as-one-resource runs a preflight 'in a sprint that changes the budget, or whose recorded budget no preflight has yet passed'; decision:suite-contracts-checked-before-a-round repeats that condition; decision:workers-sized-per-machine says each machine keeps its own worker count in 'A record outside the committed tree, kept on the machine', and that 'The preflight and the budget planner read the record' and lower the count where the machine cannot carry the budget. The corpus does not say whether 'no preflight has yet passed' means on any machine or on this machine: reading B narrows the skip, reading A keeps it as written. Harm the filer had in view: a second developer's machine, short of the budget's memory, skips the preflight on another machine's pass and meets the shortfall in a whole-suite round (cost the preflight decision exists to avoid); no accept-list entry needed, this is a product-intent choice. Options: A a pass on any machine counts, the committed mark alone skips; cost: a machine that never ran the stack under the budget skips its preflight, and workers-sized-per-machine's lowered count is never written before the first round on that machine. B (built) a pass counts per machine, recorded in the git-ignored cache; cost: every machine, and every fresh clone or cleaned cache, pays one preflight (minutes) per budget, and the corpus should name the per-machine record in test-stack-budgeted-as-one-resource and suite-contracts-checked-before-a-round. C every sprint that names a test stack runs a preflight; cost: minutes per sprint even on an unchanged budget, and the mark becomes dead. A fourth option the filer missed: keep A's committed skip but have the first tests run on a machine with no workers-sized-per-machine record run the machine measurement instead of a full preflight; cost: the suite-contract checks (lock timing, setup twice, scratch resource) then run once per project, not per machine. Siblings: none in this batch; preflight-refile-keeps-earlier-form-prompt touches the same stage_preflight but a different question.

- i12: docs-stamp-rerun-after-dropped-claim: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs:cmd_stamp (L890-L946) writes each docspec's state (L940-L942) before review.record_closes (L944), so a stop between them leaves new stamps and ledgers with no closed-record entry, and a rerun is allowed. later_commits_bearing (L876-L887) builds ledgers from read_state, i.e. the ledger the first pass already rewrote (planned_ledgers L581-L582), plus this run's held claims. A docspec counts as bearing (bearing_docspecs L585-L598) from change_reasons on its references and listed classes, or from a ledger claim whose file changed between the planned commit and the parent of --commit. ledger_after (L859-L867) drops a claim whose doc file is gone or whose recheck this run cut. So where the first pass stamped a docspec at the planned commit only because of such a claim, the rerun no longer finds it bearing, sets new_stamp to --commit (L915-L917), and, since old_stamp (the planned commit) differs, diffs planned..parent for stale claims (L919-L923). The fixer's narrow guard is the old_stamp != new_stamp test at L919; the filed problem still matches the code. Mechanism worth giving the author: in the residual case no remaining ledger claim rests on a file changed in planned..parent (any such claim would have made the docspec bearing on the rerun too), and change_reasons does not read the ledger, so the planned..parent diff drops nothing and the rerun loses no recheck; the only difference from the first pass is the stamp value (planned vs --commit), i.e. the rerun is not idempotent, and the next docs window opens later for that docspec. Corpus: decision:docspec-stamp-opens-the-window says the stamp is 'the commit at which its documentation last passed a documentation sprint' and that 'The stamp, the claim ledger, and the owner's worked example are run state ... written only by the documentation sprint's tool'; decision:documentation-claim-ledger says 'the ledger never holds a claim no checker confirmed at its stamp'; story:keep-documentation-current promises documentation that describes the product as it stands. None says what a rerun after a stop must stamp. Harm: no accept-list entry clearly covers the residual case as analysed above (A1 half-changed state is arguable: a stop between write_state and record_closes leaves state no complete run would produce only where the rerun stamps differently); state it as the owner's choice. Options: A. record the writing documentation sprint in each docspec's run state and have a rerun keep the planned-commit stamp that sprint wrote; cost: a new run-state field every docspec's state carries, and a run-state format change (stored state, a release boundary) for a rare stop. B. read each docspec's pre-stamp state from the closing commit (--commit) and stamp from it; cost: a git read per docspec on every stamp, and the closing commit holds the pre-stamp doc-state only because the owner commits before stamping, which the stamp must then assume. C. keep the narrow guard; cost: a rerun after a stop between the state write and the close record may stamp at --commit where the first pass stamped at the planned commit, which by the analysis above loses no recheck. D (filer missed): make the stamp atomic with the close, writing every doc-state file and the closed-record entry as one temp-then-rename step per plumbline-coding rule 3.1, so no rerun follows a partial stamp; cost: a stop mid-stamp still needs a rerun when the rename sequence itself spans several files. Siblings: none of this batch.

The filed facts hold. Mechanism: (1) a conversion moves files to fixed paths (true-up:conversion_pairs L4201-4206 joins history with each source name), so a retry of a failed conversion records the same names again; (2) scripts/review:record_closes (L1933-1937) refuses any entry the ledger already lists ('the closed-record ledger ... already lists ...'), so with no rollback every later /ok refuses at the retried conversion unless something treats the stale name as free. A fourth option the filer missed: record the names after a successful move instead of before (no rollback needed); cost: breaks archive-read-by-nothing's 'bookkeeping before the move' and a crash between move and record leaves files the ledger does not list (A1).
